title: Why gas prices rise fast but fall slow #shorts
description:
In January, a gallon of regular gas cost about $2.78. By May it hit $4.50, and it's still around $4.27. So where is all that money going, and when will it come down?
Full video on the Coin Theory channel.

Data: Gasoline and diesel prices (EIA: GASREGW, GASDESW), WTI crude (EIA: DCOILWTICO), CPI and energy CPI (BLS: CPIAUCSL, CPIENGSL), retrieved from FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, through October 2026. Strait of Hormuz share of world oil: EIA, World Oil Transit Chokepoints. First-quarter oil price jump and production cuts: EIA, Today in Energy (April 2026). War timeline and tanker attacks: CNN (March 9 and October 8, 2026). Federal gas tax: 18.4 cents per gallon (US Federal Highway Administration). US as top oil producer: EIA.

This video is for education only and is not financial advice.
Original script, characters and animation. Narrated with an AI voice.
